I got myself the Gigabyte MO32U24 as my first ever OLED monitor (QD OLED). It's quite the experience, I'm happy with it!

However, the Peak1000 mode with Hypernits is a bit of a double edged sword. For gaming, it seems to work fine faking the 1000 nits so far. But when browsing the internet, I encounter the limitations behind this "magic". Whenever I visit a bright site, suddenly all the bright elements, including browser UI and windows taskbar, get darker. That's because hypernits can't keep up with completely bright pictures - the monitor still only has the roughly ~530 nits to spare on the screen. Seems a bit "muddy" in direct comparison when switching from a darker site or one with more contrasts to a bright site. 

Is there a way on Windows 11 to have HDR turn on only for games, and for the desktop to remain SDR?

And again: This "issue" doesn't appear in gaming so far. Completely bright images are very rare in games - and even if so: Maybe it's a good thing to not actually get flashed with 1000 nits by an ingame flashbang ;)

I am still considering turning off the Peak1000 mode though. Still undecided. The "regular" HDR, while more consistent, is a bit dark.
